title: Conversation-slope coalescer: adaptive coalescing to reduce KV pressure and GPU fragmentation for streaming chat
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a new batch formation heuristic (Conversation-Slope Coalescer) for streaming chat completions that adapts coalescing aggressiveness based on per-conversation token generation slope, GPU slab utilization, and KV cache pressure. Goal: reduce memory fragmentation and KV churn while maintaining token-latency SLOs for low-latency streaming responses.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end P99 token latency for streaming chat routes does not regress more than 5% compared to baseline under synthetic conversational load
2) Average GPU memory fragmentation metric reduced by >=12% for mixed short+long session workload
3) KV cache hit rate improves by >=8% for conversations with interleaved short turns
4) No increase in tail CPU usage on router plane >10%
5) Feature gated behind a runtime flag and covered by canary rollout with rollback path
implementation_notes: Heuristic uses a sliding 60s per-conversation token slope (tokens/s) and combines it with node-level slab occupancy to compute a coalesce_score. Low slope => more aggressive coalescing (merge short partials into batch), high slope => prioritize low-latency single-request dispatch. Add a 'kv_pin' TTL (200ms) for recently used KV slots to prevent premature eviction during aggressive coalescing. Implement early-exit when batch_size >= max_tokens_per_batch or estimated_gpu_alloc + slab_padding > slab_capacity. Integrate with existing backpressure signals from autoscaler and streaming-prefetch module. Telemetry hooks: batch_size_histogram, coalesce_score_gauge, kv_pin_evictions, slab_fragmentation_estimate.
experiments_and_metrics: Local perf run (A/B) with 10k simulated users: P50 token latency +3%, P95 +6% under aggressive coalescing; after tuning slope_alpha, P95 within +2%
GPU fragmentation estimate (internal metric) dropped 15% in mixed workload run (50% short-turns, 50% long generations)
KV cache hit rate increased 9% on short-turn-heavy traffic in staging (kv_pin TTL 200ms)
Memory alloc churn (nvml_allocs/sec) down 18% on coalesced runs
CPU router overhead increased 4% due to additional scoring logic; acceptable under SLO
decisions: Use per-conversation slope (tokens/s) instead of raw token-count to capture burstiness and steady streaming behaviors
Implement kv_pin TTL as a short-term mitigation rather than complex LRU shard changes to reduce risk and rollout complexity
Expose coalesce_alpha and slope_window as runtime-configurable knobs for rapid tuning in canary
Cap aggressive coalescing when node slab occupancy > 78% to avoid OOM risk
open_questions: Should kv_pin be pinned per-slot or per-conversation? Current implementation pins per-slot; may cause over-pin in multi-turn parallel convos
Edge-case: interactions with prefetching for long-context completions; prefetch may be starved if coalescing merges too many short requests
We need product guidance on acceptable P95 regression under 99% of customer traffic for default-on behavior
review_feedback: PM (Anika Patel): prefer conservative default to avoid product-visible regressions; require canary at 10% traffic before ramp
Design (Rafael Ortiz): UX-level note to document potential short-latency spikes when slope flips rapidly
SRE (Priya Nair): add automated rollback if OOM events spike >2x during canary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive coalescing increases token-latency tail. Mitigation: adaptive thresholds, canary + traffic shadowing, runtime knobs
Risk: kv_pin increases KV memory footprint. Mitigation: conservative TTL (200ms) and eviction budget counter per-node
Risk: scheduler CPU overhead. Mitigation: move scoring hot-path to C++ runtime hook and micro-optimize coalesce calculation
